_tile: The second Bedroom, Saint-Remy, September 1889 -- the full-size repetition he made for himself after the first was water-damaged. Same three tiles as bedroom1 and deliberately at the same canvas fractions, because the question this station asks is whether the two are the same room.
_canvas_cm: 92.3 x 73.6 from the Art Institute of Chicago's open-access API for 1926.417 -- which is a conversion of 36 1/4 x 29 inches, and rounded inches are why it disagrees with the scan. The scan's aspect is 1.2815 against the catalogue's 1.2541: 2.2%, the second worst in the set. The shape used downstream is the scan's and the size is the catalogue's, which is M5's correction.
_px_per_cm: This scan is 78 px/cm and the working image is 120, so it is resampled UP by 1.54x. That invents no detail and it is done anyway, because every scale constant below is in px at 120 px/cm and a canvas measured at a different scale cannot be compared with one measured at this one -- and comparing the three Bedrooms is the entire reason this canvas is here. What it costs is fewer and smoother strokes than the other two, which is a fact about the reproduction.
